  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Fork PRs run the check, and fetching the merge commit from origin can fail, causing CI to fail even when the PR has no agents.md violations.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines 263-270 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The check executes the checker from the PR checkout, so a PR can modify the checker to pass while directly editing agents.md.
  WHY: The gate runs code from the same merge commit it is intended to check, allowing a PR to disable its enforcement.
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: lines 78-84 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: An insertion hunk that starts with a `## Repo-tree (auto-generated)` heading can be classified as belonging to the exempt section, causing the entire hunk, including arbitrary prose, to be skipped.
  WHY: The reviewers disagree on severity (NIT vs MAJOR); the highest severity is MAJOR because this bypass lets direct documentation additions pass the gate.
- tests/test_check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: line 166 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The prompt-extraction test hardcodes the heredoc terminator indentation and can extract the rest of the workflow when that indentation changes, allowing its substring assertions to pass without validating the extracted prompt.
  WHY: The test does not verify that the terminator was found or that the extracted prompt is correctly bounded.
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: lines 70-74 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When agents.md is deleted between base and head, the path is silently skipped and the summary reports no added content, making deletion indistinguishable from no change.
  WHY: The script omits the deleted path from its totals, so its `outcome=ok net_added=...` summary does not reveal the removal.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: `check()`: `section = _section_of_line(new_lines, start if added else start + 1)` followed by `if section == GENERATED_SECTION: continue` | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: An insert-only hunk whose first added line is a `## Repo-tree (auto-generated)` heading is attributed to the exempt section, so the whole hunk is skipped, including any prose after the heading.
  WHY: A PR can add a block that starts with that heading, followed by arbitrary documentation; the checker prints `outcome=ok` and exits 0.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines 260-261 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The CI check runs for fork PRs where origin might not be reachable or configured for the main repository, causing git fetch to fail.
  WHY: A fork PR will fail the static-checks CI step with a git fetch error (reason=git_failed) even when the PR diff has no violations to check.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: line 265 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The enforcement script runs directly from the untrusted PR checkout.
  WHY: A PR can modify scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py to always return 0 (success), effectively bypassing the agents.md direct-edit check while potentially adding new documentation to agents.md directly.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines 259-261, the new `if:` predicate `github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !(github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && github.base_ref == github.event.repository.default_branch && (startsWith(github.head_ref, 'orchestrator/project-') || startsWith(github.head_ref, 'auto/forward-merge-stable-')))` | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The step runs for fork PRs and the fetch can fail because origin does not have the fork tip parent.
  WHY: The fetch failure surfaces as `::error::AGENTS_MD_DIRECT_EDIT outcome=error reason=git_failed` and fails CI even when the PR has zero `agents.md` changes.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines 262-269, the `run:` block of the new step which calls `python3 scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py` from the checkout | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The checker executes from the PR checkout rather than a verified workflow-support SHA.
  WHY: A PR can edit the checker and agents.md together, causing the gate to pass without enforcing the §30 contract.
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: lines 50-58 (`_section_of_line`) and lines 78-84 (`section = _section_of_line(new_lines, start if added else start + 1)` / `if section == GENERATED_SECTION: continue`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A trailing insertion hunk can be attributed to an existing Repo-tree heading and exempted, allowing a new Repo-tree heading and arbitrary prose to bypass the gate.
  WHY: The preceding `assemble_agents.py check` validates pending fragments, not the agents file's Repo-tree section.
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: lines 70-74, the `try: new_lines = _git(repo_root, "show", f"{head}:{path}") ... except RuntimeError: continue` block | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When agents.md is deleted between base and head, the path is silently skipped with no totals entry or violation.
  WHY: The summary reports `outcome=ok net_added=none`, so a reader cannot distinguish an unchanged file from a removed one.
- tests/test_check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: `test_prompts_the_pipeline_sends_name_the_fragment_rule` lines 163-164 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The heredoc split hardcodes the closing `EOF` indentation, so an indentation change can make extraction return the whole workflow body.
  WHY: The substring assertions may pass trivially or fail without a useful diagnostic.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: Lines 268-269 run `scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py` from the checked-out workspace. | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The check runs the PR’s version of the checker, not a trusted version.
  WHY: A PR that adds direct documentation to `agents.md` can also change the checker to return success, defeating the enforcement this change adds.
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: Lines 78-80, especially `_section_of_line(new_lines, start if added else start + 1)`. | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Section classification includes the first added line in the hunk; if an insertion adds a `## Repo-tree (auto-generated)` heading followed by documentation, that heading classifies the entire insertion hunk as exempt.
  WHY: The checker skips that hunk and reports success, allowing directly added documentation outside the actual generated tree content to pass CI.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: lines 52-58 (`_section_of_line`) and line 82 (`section = _section_of_line(new_lines, start if added else start + 1)`) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When a pure-insertion hunk's first added line recreates the `## Repo-tree (auto-generated)` heading, `_section_of_line` attributes the entire hunk to that section and skips it.
  WHY: A PR can add that heading followed by arbitrary prose as one insert-only hunk and pass the check.
- tests/test_check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: line 166 (`workflow.split('cat > "${PROMPT_TEMPLATE_FILE}" <<\'EOF\'', 1)[1].split("\n          EOF\n", 1)[0]`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test hardcodes the heredoc terminator indentation and does not verify the extracted prompt is non-empty.
  WHY: If the heredoc indentation changes, extraction can include the entire rest of the file and the substring assertions still pass.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines 263-270, step "agents.md direct-edit check (CLAUDE.md §30)", specifically `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py \` | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The enforcement step executes the checker from the PR checkout, so a PR can modify the checker and agents.md in the same commit and pass the direct-edit check.
  WHY: CI checks out GITHUB_SHA, the PR merge commit, before the step runs, so the invocation resolves to the PR-head copy of the checker.
- scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: lines 50-56 (`_section_of_line`) and line 78 (`section = _section_of_line(new_lines, start if added else start + 1)`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: For an insertion hunk, the section lookup includes the first added line; recreating the `## Repo-tree (auto-generated)` heading therefore causes the whole hunk to be attributed to the exempt section.
  WHY: The preceding `assemble_agents.py check` step validates pending `agents.d/` fragments, not the agents file's Repo-tree section.
- tests/test_check_agents_md_direct_edits.py: line 166, `inline_prompt = workflow.split('cat > "${PROMPT_TEMPLATE_FILE}" <<\'EOF\'', 1)[1].split("\n          EOF\n", 1)[0]` | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test hardcodes the heredoc terminator indentation and never asserts the extracted prompt is non-empty or that the terminator was found.
  WHY: If a future edit changes the run-block indentation or terminator, extraction can include the rest of the workflow and the substring assertions still pass.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
